newsitem.title: USA: US Rep Kennedy pushes plan for heating oil stocks.
newsitem.headline: US Rep Kennedy pushes plan for heating oil stocks.

text.p: U.S. Representative Joseph Kennedy II (D-Mass) Tuesday unveiled a plan to increase home heating oil inventories to avert possible abrupt price hikes during the cold winter months.

During a press conference at a Boston heating oil depot, Kennedy called on the Clinton Administration to sell off Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) crude oil and buy home heating oil to be released into the market in case of price spikes this winter.
"The stage may be set for a significant increase in retail prices for home heating oil and diesel fuel over the next several months," Kennedy said.

The plan comes at a time of extremely low heating oil stock levels. Weekly reports by the Energy Information Administration and American Petroleum Institute show refiners' distillate inventories hovering 15 percent below five-year averages for this time of year.
In the key East Coast region, distillate inventories are running 30 percent below year-ago levels.
Kennedy said the low inventory leaves cold-weather states vulnerable to price hikes as high as 20 cents per gallon in case of severe cold.

"This could mean the average family having to pay $200 more this winter to keep warm. The impact would be felt by all consumers, but the burden would fall particularly hard on low income households and senior citizens, Kennedy said.
Kennedy joined 21 senators and 19 representatives in sending a letter last Wednesday to Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary, asking whether the government could sell SPR crude to stem steep price jumps.
